text: Before writing code, the agent asks what you are really trying to do and talks through a plan with you
quote: it *doesn't* just jump into trying to write code. Instead, it steps back and asks you what you're really trying to do.

text: Produces an implementation plan detailed enough for a junior engineer with no context or judgement to follow
quote: your agent puts together an implementation plan that's clear enough for an enthusiastic junior engineer with poor taste, no judgement, no project context, and an aversion to testing to follow

text: Implementation plans emphasize red/green TDD, YAGNI and DRY
quote: It emphasizes true red/green TDD, YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It), and DRY.

text: Enforces red/green TDD: write a failing test first, then only enough code to make it pass
quote: Claude practices RED/GREEN TDD, writing a failing test, implementing only enough code to make that test pass, and then moving on.

text: Subagent-driven development dispatches tasks one by one to subagents and reviews each task before moving on
quote: this month's cool new process, where it dispatches tasks one by one to subagents to implement and then code reviews each task before continuing.

text: Lets you choose between a manual second-session PM workflow and the automated subagent workflow
quote: it offers you a choice between: 1. last month's process (where you'd open a second `claude` session and act as a human PM...) 2. this month's cool new process, where it dispatches tasks one by one to subagents to implement and then code rev

text: The agent can work autonomously for a couple of hours without deviating from the agreed plan
quote: It's not uncommon for your agent to work autonomously for a couple hours at a time without deviating from the plan you put together.

text: Classifies requests as spike, bounded or architectural so small tasks skip the full two-document process
quote: Ceremony now scales to the task. Requests are classified as spike, bounded, or architectural; small tasks skip the two-document ritual.

text: Does quick tasks right away, agrees small changes in chat and writes a design doc for projects; you can override its call
quote: It does a quick, clear task right away, agrees a small change with you in chat, and writes a design document for a project. You can override its call

text: Every workflow path stops for your approval before implementation begins
quote: Every path still stops for your approval before implementation.

text: Non-catastrophic conflicts get a recorded ruling and work continues; only destructive or irreversible actions stop for a human
quote: Non-catastrophic conflicts and ambiguities get a recorded ruling and work continues; only destructive or irreversible actions still stop for a human.

text: Batches small same-shape tasks into one subagent dispatch to cut cost, and batch reviews check every briefed file is in the diff
quote: Small same-shape tasks batch into one dispatch, cutting subagent cost sharply on micro-task plans; batch reviews verify every file in the brief made it into the diff.

text: Worktree removal stops and lists uncommitted files to ask you instead of using --force
quote: Worktree removal no longer destroys untracked files. When `git worktree remove` refuses because the tree holds uncommitted work, the skill stops, names the files, and asks

text: Uses a plan-scoped workspace directory per plan, deleted once the final review is clean
quote: `sdd-workspace` now requires the plan file and resolves a per-plan directory, `.superpowers/sdd//`; ... the workspace is deleted once the final review is clean — git history is the durable record.

text: Review-fix rounds resume the original implementer and use a scoped re-review prompt
quote: The review-fix loop resumes the implementer. The lifecycle restructure gives fix rounds resume-the-implementer semantics instead of fresh dispatches, adds a scoped re-review prompt

text: Review-fix loop has a five-round circuit breaker with controller adjudication when it trips
quote: The review-fix loop resumes the implementer... installs a five-round circuit breaker with controller adjudication when it trips.

text: Plans carry a Spec pointer that is read at setup, so plan conflicts are resolved against the design
quote: Plans carry a `Spec:` pointer and SDD reads the spec at setup, so plan conflicts get resolved against the design instead of guessed at.

text: A pre-dispatch conflict scan records its checks in a ledger
quote: The pre-dispatch conflict scan records its checks in the ledger instead of just asserting the plan is clean.

text: Implementer and reviewer subagents are barred from spawning their own subagents to avoid duplicate reviews
quote: Implementers and reviewers may not spawn their own subagents, which was producing duplicate reviews.

text: Includes a code-reviewer agent that checks implementations against plans, coding standards and architectural principles
quote: The framework includes a code-reviewer agent that evaluates implementations against plans, coding standards, and architectural principles.

text: Automatically creates and switches to a git worktree after brainstorming, so parallel tasks do not clobber each other
quote: After you're done brainstorming, if you're in a git repo it automatically creates a worktree for the project and changes to that directory. This means that you can start parallel tasks on the same project that don't clobber each other.

text: At the end of implementation it offers to open a GitHub PR, merge the worktree locally, or stop
quote: At the end of the implementation process, Claude will now offer to make a GitHub pull request, merge the worktree back to the source branch locally, or just stop.

text: Four-phase debugging methodology that requires root-cause investigation before any fix
quote: a four-phase debugging methodology that requires root cause investigation before any fixes

text: Triggers an architectural review after three failed fix attempts
quote: a four-phase debugging methodology that requires root cause investigation before any fixes... with safeguards that trigger architectural review after three failed fix attempts

text: Routes bug-fix requests to the systematic-debugging skill before domain skills
quote: "Fix this bug" → superpowers:systematic-debugging first, then domain skills.

text: Brainstorming plays back its understanding of each part in a few hundred words and marks its guesses as guesses
quote: As it understands each part, it plays that part back in a few hundred words and marks its guesses as guesses.

text: The first brainstorming message offers to skip the questions and asks one open, concrete question
quote: Its first message offers to skip the questions and asks one open question about a real moment or a concrete picture.

text: A fresh subagent reads the design as its implementer and lists the questions it would still need answered
quote: A fresh subagent reads the design as the person who'll build it and lists what they'd still need to ask.

text: Offers to research prior art, your project, or the web during brainstorming
quote: Along the way, it offers to look at prior art, your project, or the web.

text: Presents the drafted spec to you in short chunks you can read and digest
quote: Once it's teased a spec out of the conversation, it shows it to you in chunks short enough to actually read and digest.

text: Slash commands such as /brainstorming and /execute-plan run requirement exploration and batched plans with review checkpoints
quote: Invoke skills with slash commands like `/brainstorming` to explore requirements and design before implementation, or `/execute-plan` to run batched implementation plans with review checkpoints.

text: Provides a skills-search tool for discovering available skills
quote:
20+ battle-tested skills
*   `/brainstorm`, `/write-plan`, `/execute-plan` commands
*   Skills-search tool for discovery

text: SessionStart context injection bootstraps the skills system at the start of each session
quote: 20+ battle-tested skills; `/brainstorm`, `/write-plan`, `/execute-plan` commands; Skills-search tool for discovery; SessionStart context injection

text: Skills trigger automatically, with no special action needed from the user
quote: because the skills trigger automatically, you don't need to do anything special. Your coding agent just has Superpowers.

text: The agent is instructed to invoke relevant skills before any response or action, including clarifying questions
quote: Invoke relevant or requested skills BEFORE any response or action — including clarifying questions, exploring the codebase, or checking files.

text: User instructions such as CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md take precedence over skills, and skills override default behavior
quote: User instructions (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, etc, direct requests) take precedence over skills, which in turn override default behavior.

text: Skills are harness-agnostic: the skills/ folder is the single source of truth, shared verbatim by every harness
quote: Skills (harness-agnostic). Everything in `skills/` is the source of truth, shared verbatim by every harness.

text: Supports many harnesses, including Claude Code, Antigravity, Codex, Cursor, Devin, Factory Droid, Gemini, Copilot CLI and OpenCode
quote: Getting Started: Claude Code, Antigravity, Codex App, Codex CLI, Cursor, Devin CLI, Factory Droid, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI ... OpenCode

text: Installation differs by harness, with a separate install for each harness you use
quote: Installation differs by harness. If you use more than one, install Superpowers separately for each one.

text: Installs into Claude Code via two plugin marketplace commands
quote:
/plugin marketplace add obra/superpowers-marketplace
/plugin install superpowers@superpowers-marketplace

text: Devin CLI install with one plugins command, with skills auto-triggering at session start
quote: Devin CLI: `devin plugins install obra/superpowers` now works, and skills auto-trigger at session start.

text: Hermes Agent install from a git clone, with skills registering in Hermes' native loader
quote: Hermes Agent: install from a git clone; skills register with Hermes' native loader and the bootstrap loads on the first turn.

text: Antigravity runs the session-start hook so skills are active from the first message; reinstalling updates it
quote: Antigravity runs the plugin's session-start hook, so Superpowers is active from the first message. Reinstall with the same command to update.

text: Ships a native plugin manifest for the Antigravity Marketplace
quote: This release also adds a native plugin manifest for the Antigravity Marketplace

text: Grok Build CLI install instructions are included in the docs
quote: Grok Build CLI added to the install docs.

text: Codex, Copilot CLI and Gemini CLI recognize ~/.agents/skills/ as a shared cross-runtime skills location
quote: Codex, Copilot CLI, and Gemini CLI all also recognize `~/.agents/skills/` as a cross-runtime alias.

text: A guide explains how to add support for new IDEs, CLIs or agent runners so skills auto-trigger there as they do natively
quote: This guide explains how to add support for a new harness — an IDE, CLI, or agent runner that isn't Claude Code — so that Superpowers skills auto-trigger there the same way they do natively.

text: Porting to a harness adds a tool-mapping reference and bootstrap injector without editing SKILL.md files
quote: Porting adds a tool-mapping reference and a bootstrap injector; it never reaches into `skills/*/SKILL.md` to swap tool names.

text: Everything installs through each harness's own install mechanism and never edits the user's files
quote: Everything ships through the harness's own install mechanism. Never edit the user's files.

text: An eval harness drives real tmux sessions of Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI, with an LLM verifier judging skill compliance
quote: evals/` — do agents behave correctly on real LLM sessions? Python harness driving real tmux sessions of Claude Code / Codex / Gemini CLI, with an LLM actor and verifier judging skill compliance.

text: Integration tests in Bash, Node and Python cover the plugin's non-LLM code
quote: tests/` — does the plugin's non-LLM code work? Bash + node + python integration tests for brainstorm-server JS, OpenCode plugin loading, codex-plugin sync, and analysis utilities.

text: Includes a writing-skills module that teaches authoring and testing new skills
quote: The writing-skills module teaches you to author and test new skills

text: Skill authoring follows TDD: write subagent pressure-scenario tests, watch them fail, write the skill, then close loopholes
quote: You write test cases (pressure scenarios with subagents), watch them fail (baseline behavior), write the skill (documentation), watch tests pass (agents comply), and refactor (close loopholes).

text: The TDD reference doc is a positive catalog of six good-test rules that lead with good examples
quote: `testing-anti-patterns.md` is now `writing-good-tests.md`. The TDD reference doc is rebuilt as a positive catalog — six rules that lead with the GOOD example
